name: Threshold Dimension of Addressing
details: Under the standard convention $n=2^d$; this corrects an off-by-one in the legacy table.
proof: Projecting to the $d=\log_2 n$ address coordinates gives the full $d$-cube.  Its chain $\emptyset,\{a_1\},\ldots,\{a_1,\ldots,a_d\}$ is realized by the address concepts; adding the primary coordinate of the all-one address concept gives one further realized trace.  Hence the threshold dimension is at least $d+1$.  Conversely, the final trace of a threshold chain is contained in one addressing concept and so uses at most its $d$ address coordinates and its single primary coordinate.  Thus no chain has dimension exceeding $d+1$.
